title: Spouses Arevalo v. Planters Development Bank
summary: The Supreme Court struck down an unconscionable interest rate imposed by a bank on a loan, ruling that while the Usury Law ceiling has been suspended, interest rates imposed must still be reasonable. Courts may reduce iniquitous or unconscionable interest rates.
doctrine: While the Usury Law has been effectively suspended by CB Circular No. 905, interest rates imposed on loans are still subject to the court's authority to reduce them when they are unconscionable. An interest rate of 36% per annum or higher is generally considered excessive and may be reduced by the courts.
fullText:
REYES, J.:

The core issue is whether the interest rate of 36% per annum imposed by the respondent bank on the loan is valid and enforceable.

While the Usury Law has been effectively repealed by Central Bank Circular No. 905, the Court has consistently held that this does not grant lenders unbridled authority to impose any rate of interest. The contractual stipulation on interest may still be struck down if it is unconscionable.

The Court has the authority to equitably reduce unreasonable interest rates. An interest rate that is excessive, unconscionable, or inequitable is void for being contrary to morals, if not against the law.
